feedback.worked_solution:
We found that $A=2$ and $B=3$ in steps 2 and 3, respectively. Hence, $f(x)={x}^{3}+2x.$ 

Using the sum and constant factor rules and our result from step 4, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{f(x)}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{{x}^{3}+2x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (1+\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 1\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x-\frac{2}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
